narrative.overview: Maestro looks like the bound working notebook of a design team, opened flat on a desk in daylight. Warm paper, ink that is brown-black rather than black, a rust accent that reads as something drawn on the page rather than something rendered on a screen. It is a reading surface first. Density is high and unapologetic: rows are 36 pixels and hierarchy is earned with weight, size and rule lines rather than with air. Two typefaces carry the whole product and divide the work by ownership: the tool speaks in Fira Sans, and the game speaks in Literata.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, never white, never grey.
Two voices: sans for the tool, serif for the game.
Rust accent, spent sparingly and never as decoration.
Flat surfaces, three shadow levels reserved for what genuinely floats.
36-pixel rows and a compact scale: comparison beats comfort.

rules.name: The Two Exemptions Rule
rules.body: The chrome is achromatic. Exactly two chromatic tokens exist outside the data palette, accent and danger, and a third is admitted only against this test: not 'would a colour help' but 'is there a fact on screen that nothing else says'.

rules.name: The Ink Button Rule
rules.body: The primary button is ink on paper. A button filled with the accent is forbidden.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: ground is darker than paper on purpose. The diagram lies on the desk; the reading panels are sheets on top of it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The tool speaks sans, the game speaks serif. If it would survive the game shipping, it is serif.

rules.name: The No Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case with light tracking. All-caps labels are the admin-panel tell.

rules.name: The Copyable Is Mono Rule
rules.body: If a value is a machine identifier a person might paste, it is monospace.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is rgba(94, 72, 55, ...), the paper's own brown. Pure black is forbidden everywhere.

rules.name: The Earned Elevation Rule
rules.body: A shadow answers a question about stacking, never about importance.

rules.name: The Named Absence Rule
rules.body: Nothing is blank because a value is missing. Absent gets a word, empty gets a different word.

rules.name: The Shadow Boundary Rule
rules.body: An element selector in the global stylesheet does not reach inside a component's shadow root, and custom properties do. No component writes a bare button rule of its own; every one adopts the shared control stylesheet written in terms of var(--...).

rules.name: The Never Hidden Rule
rules.body: Navigation is never hidden without being moved somewhere reachable. Below 780px the destinations join the game switcher's menu; exactly one of the two carries them at any width.

dos: Do set every game-owned word in Literata and every tool-owned word in Fira Sans.
Do keep rows at 36px and lists dense.
Do tint every shadow with rgba(94, 72, 55, ...).
Do name absences in words: 'no zone', 'never reviewed', 'no requirement'.
Do state read-only where the missing action would be.
Do mark the current item with weight and aria-current.
Do build every repeated pattern once, as a shared component.
Do cap prose at 68ch, and nothing else.
Do let wide content scroll inside its own container so the page never scrolls sideways.
Do put a breadcrumb on every screen inside a game, and delete the back links it replaces.
donts: Don't build the generic admin panel: no icon sidebar, no card grid of counters.
Don't reach for the dark blue SaaS dashboard.
Don't bury content the way the ad-choked game wiki does.
Don't produce the empty beautiful landing page.
Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere, including in a shadow.
Don't fill a button, a badge or a header with the accent.
Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a coloured stripe.
Don't set a label in all caps.
Don't nest a panel inside a panel.
Don't leave a cell blank when the value is absent.
Don't animate layout properties, and never use bounce or elastic easing.
Don't add a modal before an inline alternative has been ruled out in writing.
Don't put a measure meant for prose on the page.
Don't hide navigation at a breakpoint without moving it somewhere.
Don't write a bare element selector for a control inside a component and expect the global stylesheet to have styled it.
